cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: The Equality Act 2010 consolidated and simplified previous anti-discrimination legislation into a single Act, replacing the Race Relations Act, Sex Discrimination Act and Disability Discrimination Act among others

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: The Act protects nine protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Direct discrimination occurs when a person is treated less favourably because of a protected characteristic (e.g. refusing a job to someone because of their race)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Indirect discrimination occurs when a provision, criterion or practice is applied to everyone but puts people with a protected characteristic at a particular disadvantage and cannot be justified as a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Harassment is unwanted conduct related to a protected characteristic that has the purpose or effect of violating a person's dignity or creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading or humiliating environment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Victimisation occurs when a person is subjected to a detriment because they have made a complaint about discrimination, supported someone else's complaint or given evidence in a discrimination case

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: The public sector equality duty under section 149 requires public authorities to have due regard to the need to eliminate discrimination, advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between different groups

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Disability discrimination includes the duty to make reasonable adjustments — employers and service providers must modify practices, premises or provisions to remove substantial disadvantage faced by disabled people

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Positive action (not positive discrimination) is permitted under the Act where people with a protected characteristic are underrepresented or disadvantaged; measures can be taken to encourage participation or overcome disadvantage

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: The Employment Tribunal hears discrimination claims in employment; the County Court hears other discrimination claims; claims must generally be brought within three months (employment) or six months (other areas)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Remedies for discrimination include compensation (which is uncapped in employment cases), recommendations for the employer to change practices, and declarations of rights

cards.front: Recall a key point about Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law
cards.back: Exemptions exist: occupational requirements allow discrimination where a characteristic is a genuine and determining requirement of the job (e.g. a Catholic school requiring a headteacher to be Catholic), and age discrimination can be justified if it is a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — equality & anti-discrimination law?
cards.back: 1. For Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Equality & Anti-Discrimination Law 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
